key_finding: Dunbrack BBdep library uses 20°×20° bins at 10° centers. Sparse region begins at φ≥−40° (very sparse at φ≥−30°, often only 1–2 crystallographic observations per bin). find_closest_angle nearest-neighbor correctly maps into the library but statistical reliability degrades sharply in φ≥−30° space.
decision: find_closest_angle nearest-neighbor is sufficient for v1. No interpolation needed. φ≥−30° is a documented low-confidence zone, not a bug.
action: Add API-doc warning to backbone_bin: 'φ≥−30° returns a bin with <3 observations; placement probability is unreliable.' Add fixture covering positive-φ backbone (fetch small RCSB structure with loop if fuserinput.pdb lacks one).

key_finding: Dunbrack library has separate cis-PRO and trans-PRO populations. Cis-PRO exclusively occupies ψ=20°–100° (rarely populated by trans-PRO), with a Cγ-endo/exo ring-pucker split at ψ=65°. The −75°<φ<−50° band has kinetic equilibrium between both forms. Single-form approximation blends these populations and produces incorrect ring puckers in cis-PRO-specific ψ regions.
decision: Debt #67 is materially important for design accuracy — not cosmetic. Single-form approximation is acceptable only for non-PRO residues. backbone_bin must accept a cis_proline flag for PRO; backbone parser must detect cis peptide from ω≈0°.
action: Elevate Debt #67 to planned. Spec update: backbone_bin(aa='PRO', phi, psi, cis=false). backbone parser extracts ω from adjacent C=O and N atoms; flags cis if |ω|<30°. Separate cis-PRO library bin set required.

key_finding: GLY has no χ1 angle and is excluded from all rotamer populations (na=0 in library). ALA has no χ1 either but its CB atom is treated as a sidechain atom — doNotCountCB is true for all AAs EXCEPT ALA. place_rotamer returns CB for all AAs; ConFind cache_residue_impl applies counts_as_sidechain to exclude CB for non-ALA at the clash-detection layer. Implementation is correct per spec.
decision: Current doNotCountCB logic in sidechain.rs and counts_as_sidechain is correct. No code changes needed. GLY na=0 sentinel and ALA CB semantics are well-handled.
action: Add explicit API doc entries: (1) 'GLY: no rotamers (na=0); place_rotamer returns Err(UnknownAa) or an empty atom list.' (2) 'ALA: CB is counted as sidechain in ConFind clash detection; all other AAs exclude CB.'
feeds: public API documentation, GLY fixture addition

key_finding: default_bin is argmax over all bin frequency values globally — the single highest-frequency conformation across the entire library. It is a sentinel fallback triggered only by φ=9999.0 or ψ=9999.0. Using default_bin with valid backbone angles ignores backbone-specific steric constraints (syn-pentane interactions with Ci-1, Ni+1, Oi) and will produce incorrect, potentially clashing placements.
decision: default_bin must never be used with valid backbone angles. API contract: backbone_bin with φ=9999.0 || ψ=9999.0 → default_bin (global mode fallback). All callers with real backbone must provide actual φ/ψ.
action: Add // Safety doc to backbone_bin sentinel check. Add test: for a known AA (e.g. LEU), assert that backbone_bin(phi=−60, psi=−40) != default_bin and that the result changes meaningfully with phi/psi variation.

key_finding: χ1=N-Cα-Cβ-Xγ; three rotamer wells (g+: 0°–120° centered ~+60°; t: 120°–240° centered ~180°; g-: −120°–0° centered ~−60°). PHE/TYR χ2 is non-rotameric (clusters ±90°) due to sp2 Cδ atoms at χ2 and χ2+180°. ASP χ2=−60° ≡ +120° by carboxylate symmetry. Eight semirotameric AAs (Asp, Asn, Gln, Glu, His, Phe, Tyr, Trp) have sp2 terminal χ treated continuously in Dunbrack 2010. ASN/GLN/HIS are frequently modeled ±180° wrong in PDB data; MolProbity Reduce corrects via H-bond network.
decision: When adding χ-angle output to PlacedRotamer, emit raw library dihedral values; document which AAs have symmetric or non-rotameric terminal χ. Normalization (fold-to-canonical) is a v2 concern.
action: No immediate code change. When PlacedRotamer gains chi_angles: Vec<f64>, add a comment: 'PHE/TYR χ2 is non-rotameric (not ±60°/180°); ASP/GLU terminal χ has 180° degeneracy; ASN/GLN/HIS may be misoriented in raw PDB — normalize before comparison.'
feeds: PlacedRotamer chi-angle extension, PDB fixture preprocessing

key_finding: Most challenging regions for rotamer placement: loops and turns (non-α/non-β) traverse sparse, irregular φ/ψ space. Worst-predicted residues: SER (57% accuracy even with BBdep), CYS, THR, ASN — hydrogen-bonding interactions override local steric predictions. Available fixtures already in /home/marielle/repos/mosaist/testfiles/: 2ZTA (leucine zipper, helical), heptad files, fuserinput.pdb (unknown content), 1DC7/1DC8 (broad AA/secondary structure coverage).

key_finding: Contact degree is sequence-independent: evaluates all 18 amino acids × all rotamers at both positions, weighted by background propensities and rotamer probabilities. Asks 'given this backbone, how likely is sidechain coupling?' — not 'are these atoms touching now?' Threshold c(i,j)>0.02 defines 'poised to interact.' Distance/vdW metrics are sequence-specific snapshots. CD captures: evolutionary coupling, genuine interaction potential (not spatial proximity alone), and positional crowdedness. Used in dTERMen to define TERM neighborhoods — positions with c(i,j)>0.02 define C in the energy model.
decision: API docs should frame CD as 'backbone-geometry coupling probability' not 'contact energy.' The 0.02 threshold is domain knowledge for downstream consumers; expose it as a named constant.
action: Add CONTACT_THRESHOLD: f64 = 0.02 as a pub const to contact_list.rs or lib.rs. Document in ContactList: 'Positions with cd > CONTACT_THRESHOLD are considered poised to interact (Zheng & Grigoryan 2017).' This is the correct downstream filter for TERM neighborhood construction.
feeds: ContactList API docs, future proxide-master TERM definition

key_finding: loCollProbCut=0.5 and hiCollProbCut=2.0 are empirically tuned geometric constants — not calibrated against B-factors or NMR order parameters. --freeB (B-factor freedom) mode exists in MSL CLI but is out of scope for v1. Freedom~0: buried/core position, most rotamers clash with backbone or neighbors — sequence is highly constrained, mutation-sensitive. Freedom~1: surface/exposed position — wide amino-acid tolerance. Denominator is numLibraryRotamers (total library, including pruned), so freedom accounts for overall backbone steric context.
decision: Do NOT expose loCollProbCut/hiCollProbCut as runtime-tunable parameters in v1. Keep as named constants. --freeB deferred to v2. Document empirical origin.
action: Ensure pub const LO_COLL_PROB_CUT: f64 = 0.5 and HI_COLL_PROB_CUT: f64 = 2.0 are defined as named constants (not magic numbers) in parallel.rs. Add doc comment: 'Empirically tuned; not calibrated against experimental flexibility measures (B-factors, NMR S²).'
feeds: freedom constant documentation, v2 --freeB feature planning

key_finding: Phase A pruning is not skippable: (1) backbone-clashing rotamers would inflate weight_of_available_rotamers (the CD denominator), diluting all CD values — physically impossible states would appear to contribute to the interaction probability; (2) backbone-clashing rotamers could generate false sidechain-sidechain contacts via states that can never exist. CLASH_DIST=2.0Å is physically grounded in vdW repulsion radii. crowdedness = fraction_pruned is a free byproduct of Phase A.
decision: CLASH_DIST=2.0Å is a hard physical threshold, not a tunable approximation. Phase A cannot be skipped for speed without breaking CD normalization. crowdedness is correctly computed as a byproduct with zero additional cost.
action: Add doc comment to cache_residue_impl: 'CLASH_DIST=2.0Å is a hard physical vdW exclusion threshold. Pruned rotamers are excluded from the CD denominator; skipping Phase A would inflate weight_of_available_rotamers and dilute all contact degrees.' No code change.

key_finding: getConstrainedContacts iterates all 18 amino-acid identities at residue A with residue B unconstrained, producing 18 conditional CD values per pair (NOT 324 — only one direction implemented). Constraint propagates by comparing which AA identities at A produce high CD with B, then restricting B's rotamer pool via collProb. Critical C++ bug: line 209 checks aaAllowedA.empty() && aaAllowedA.empty() (checks A twice, not A and B) — replicated in Rust for parity. seq_const is deferred for v1.
decision: seq_const remains out of scope for v1. When implemented, the C++ bug must be either: (a) replicated exactly for full parity, or (b) intentionally diverged and documented as a parity exception. The bug affects the no-restriction fast path, not the constrained path itself.
action: Add comment to the replicated bug site in Rust: '// Replicates MSL C++ bug (contactDegree line 209): checks aa_allowed_a twice instead of aa_allowed_a && aa_allowed_b. Required for numerical parity on unconstrained CD path.' Open backlog item for seq_const v2 implementation.

key_finding: Rosetta packer: physics-based, pairwise-decomposable LJ+electrostatic+solvation+hbond energies precomputed for all rotamer pairs, then Metropolis MC simulated annealing. dTERMen: ConFind contact degree defines TERM neighborhoods (C = {j : c(i,j)>0.02}), MASTER searches PDB for backbone RMSD matches, sequence statistics of matches → sEPs and pEPs (statistical energy parameters), optimization against statistical model. Key divergence: Rosetta requires pairwise-decomposable energy; dTERMen's higher-order sub-TERMs implicitly capture multi-body coupling that pairwise-additive models miss.
decision: Roadmap confirmed: ConFind is layer 2 (topology). Layer 3 is MASTER-style backbone substructure search (RMSD over fragment database). Layer 4 is dTERMen sequence optimization from PDB statistics. Next crate after proxide-confind is proxide-master (not a Rosetta packer clone).
action: Add backlog item: [P2] proxide-master — backbone RMSD substructure search over a curated PDB fragment library. Depends on: proxide-confind for TERM segment set definition (contact graph → which residue segments to include in a TERM). Interface: TERM → Vec<PdbMatch> with RMSD and sequence.
feeds: roadmap: next crate, proxide-master backlog item

key_finding: Modern tools use ONE high-quality BBdep library (Dunbrack 2010/2011), not a registry of swappable libraries. Resolution is adjusted at runtime via 'extra rotamers' (-ex1, -ex2 flags that expand rotamer wells), not by library swapping. Dunbrack 2002→2010 was a one-time historical upgrade. BBdep vs. BBind selection is path-based in MSL (directory→BBdep, file→BBind). Dunbrack 2010 adds semirotameric treatment for 8 AAs (Asp, Asn, Gln, Glu, His, Phe, Tyr, Trp) with continuous terminal χ distributions.
decision: RotlibRegistry abstraction is definitively deferred. Architecture: single RotamerLibrary::load() (BBdep) plus optional RotamerLibrary::load_independent() (BBind). Extra-rotamer expansion is a wrapper that adds perturbations around rotamer well centers, not a second library. No registry needed for v1 or v2.
action: Close RotlibRegistry as a design decision: document in Debt #67 spec update — 'Single-library, runtime-expandable architecture confirmed by literature precedent (Rosetta, MSL). RotlibRegistry deferred indefinitely. Extra-rotamer expansion is a future v3 feature implemented as a post-load rotamer augmentation step.'
feeds: RotlibRegistry architecture decision, Debt #67 spec update
